ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The distribution of wetlands is affected by many factors such as climate, terrain, hydrology, and human activities. Read the line graph of wetland distribution and aridity in the Yellow River Basin (aridity is the ratio of annual evaporation to annual precipitation). <image1> The aridity of the lower Yellow River Basin is mainly between 1.5~3. According to the figure and text information, what does the size of wetland area in the lower Yellow River mainly depend on?

claims.canonical_value: The size of wetland area mainly depends on the size of upstream inflow

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a line graph of "wetland distribution and aridity in the Yellow River Basin"; the horizontal axis is aridity grading, including 0~1.5, 1.5~3, 3~7, >7; the vertical axis is wetland rate. The legend shows four types of lines: all wetlands, river wetlands, lake wetlands, and marsh wetlands. The question stem points out that the aridity of the lower Yellow River Basin is mainly between 1.5~3; within this interval, the value of river wetlands is relatively high among the individual wetland types, indicating that river wetlands are an important component. Then reason: the lower Yellow River is located on a river alluvial plain, and wetland area is closely related to river hydrological recharge. The downstream area's own precipitation and aridity conditions cannot alone determine the wetland scale, while the river water volume of the lower Yellow River is mainly controlled by inflow from the upper and middle reaches. Therefore, the size of wetland area in the lower Yellow River mainly depends on the size of upstream inflow.
